answers.answer: Resolution without conflating the two frames: my reopen-condition 'the line shifts to cotton -> redirect to Tirupur' is written for the EXPORT-COST frame — i.e. when the GOVERNING PRIORITY becomes cheap-high-volume COTTON-knit EXPORT, Tirupur (the cotton-export superior) wins. It is triggered by the priority+volume+fibre-dominance flip, NOT merely by the PRESENCE of cotton fibre in a mixed capsule. Our actual line is A1 cotton-BLEND core + A2 acrylic + A3 merino-lambswool, governed by the PRODUCT-FIT frame (small AI-designed D2C micro-brand, low volume, California margin capture, product/iteration/downstream-margin priority). Under that frame the A1 cotton-blend does NOT trip the reopen-condition, because: (1) the priority is product-fit not cost-per-unit at volume; (2) volume stays micro-MOQ, not the high-volume cotton-export case Tirupur serves; (3) it is a cotton-BLEND inside a woollen/acrylic-anchored capsule, not a pure-cotton commodity line. The reopen-condition fires only if ALL of priority->cost, line->cotton-dominant, and volume->outgrows-micro-MOQ move together. HONEST TENSION: my spec's reopen-condition text says 'the line shifts to cotton' without explicitly qualifying 'pure-cotton, cost-frame, at volume', so an adversary CAN read a cotton-blend A1 as ambiguously tripping it. The resolution is sound (frames not conflated) but the spec wording is under-specified for a MIXED-fibre line and would read more cleanly as 'shifts to a cost-driven, pure-cotton, high-volume export line'. [ESTIMATE, med-high on the location placement; frame-bound verdict]
